statement: The d02 workpack's checklist says the ratchet gate should be 'implemented as an enforcer-scan Validator/mode' — but enforcer_validator::validator::Validator is a strictly per-file, single-RuleId contract (fn validate(&self, input: ValidationInput) -> Vec<Finding> over one file's source text). The baseline ratchet is inherently cross-file and whole-run (it set-diffs an entire scan's Violation list against a persisted baseline), so it CANNOT implement that trait without either faking a per-file signature or losing the whole-run comparison. Resolved by adding a standalone BaselineRatchetValidator::gate(prior: &Baseline, current_violations: &[Violation]) -> BaselineGateOutcome — a Report-level classifier, not a Validator impl — and documenting the mismatch explicitly in the module doc comment rather than silently deviating.
why: The workpack phrasing ('Validator/mode') is deliberately loose to allow either shape, but a future reader grepping for 'impl Validator for BaselineRatchetValidator' would find nothing and might assume the requirement was skipped.
howToApply: When a workpack asks for a 'Validator/mode' or similar dual-shape requirement and the concrete trait in scope (enforcer_validator::validator::Validator) does not fit the requirement's actual granularity (per-file vs whole-report), pick the shape that matches the DATA (here: Report/Vec<Violation> in, classified Vec<Finding> out) and name the mismatch in the module doc, rather than distorting the trait's contract or skipping the requirement.

statement: enforcer-scan depends on enforcer-domain/enforcer-core/sha2 at runtime but NOT enforcer-rules (enforcer-rules depends on nothing scan-related; the dependency only goes lang-* -> enforcer-rules, never enforcer-scan -> enforcer-rules). The d02 checklist's 'baseline entries reference real registry RuleIds -- parity enforced via the d01 mechanization oracle' requirement therefore cannot be a runtime check inside baseline_ratchet.rs itself (RuleId is just a branded string newtype there, validated for SHAPE not for registry membership) -- it has to be a dev-dependency test-time check: added enforcer-rules as a [dev-dependencies] entry in crates/enforcer-scan/Cargo.toml and wrote a test that loads the real crates/enforcer-rules/rules/no-reexports.json catalog via enforcer_rules::loader::load_registry_from_files and asserts each fixture's RuleId resolves via registry.get().
why: Adding enforcer-rules as a full [dependencies] entry would create scan->rules coupling nothing else in the workspace has and that the crate's own Cargo.toml description doesn't mention; dev-dependency keeps the parity check test-only, matching how enforcer-mechanization (d01) is the actual owner of registry-wide parity.
howToApply: When a workpack requires 'real registry RuleId parity' but the owning crate's runtime dependency graph does not include enforcer-rules, add enforcer-rules ONLY as a [dev-dependencies] entry and prove parity in an integration test that loads a real catalog JSON file (not a synthetic RuleRecord), rather than promoting it to a runtime dependency or skipping the check.

statement: enforcer-core has no plain single-snapshot JSON file read/write helper -- ndjson_writer.rs is explicitly append-only (OpenOptions::append(true), grows forever, never truncates) and is the wrong primitive for a baseline file that must be OVERWRITTEN each 'enforcer check --baseline write' run (a shrinking baseline that only ever appended would never actually shrink on disk). hash_chain.rs's link_digest(prev, payload) is reusable as-is for a single-record integrity hash by calling it with prev=None (genesis-only, no chain needed for a one-shot snapshot).
why: Reaching for ndjson_writer::NdjsonWriter by pattern-matching 'enforcer-core has a JSON persistence util' would silently break the ratchet's shrink guarantee -- append-only storage cannot represent 'this baseline is now smaller than before' without reading+filtering the whole history on every load, which the existing API does not do automatically.
howToApply: For any persisted record that must be OVERWRITTEN (a snapshot/baseline/current-state file, as opposed to an event log), use std::fs::write directly (as write_baseline in crates/enforcer-scan/src/rules/baseline_ratchet.rs does) rather than enforcer_core::ndjson_writer, and reuse enforcer_core::hash_chain::link_digest(None, payload) for a standalone integrity hash without needing the chain-of-previous-digests machinery.
